answer_text:
Let the common remainder be \(r\). Then

\[
1059 \equiv 1417 \equiv 2312 \pmod d
\]

So \(d\) must divide the differences:

\[
1417-1059 = 358
\]
\[
2312-1417 = 895
\]
\[
2312-1059 = 1253
\]

Thus \(d\) divides

\[
\gcd(358,895,1253)
\]

Compute:

\[
\gcd(358,1253)
\]

Since

\[
1253 = 3(358) + 179
\]
and
\[
358 = 2(179),
\]

we get

\[
\gcd(358,1253)=179.
\]

Now check \(895\):

\[
895 = 5(179)
\]

so \(179\) also divides \(895\). Therefore,

\[
\gcd(358,895,1253)=179.
\]

Since \(d>1\), we have

\[
d=179.
\]

Verification:

\[
1059 \equiv 164 \pmod{179}
\]
\[
1417 \equiv 164 \pmod{179}
\]
\[
2312 \equiv 164 \pmod{179}
\]

Thus the answer is

\[
\boxed{179}
\]
